items.title: ROS Discourse General: What happened to "Robot-as-a-Snap"?
items.summary: Canonical has developed an Ubuntu Robotics ecosystem using Snaps and Ubuntu Core, offering atomic updates and version linking for reliable robot deployment. This ecosystem includes ROS 2 extensions, observability hooks, and fleet management tools. Despite these technical advantages, there is limited discussion in the ROS 2 community about using Snaps for production robot software deployment. Alternatives like standard apt, Docker, or Yocto are currently more commonly discussed for shipping robots. The article questions if strict confinement hinders necessary hardware access or if maintenance overhead favors other methods.
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: What happened to \"Robot-as-a-Snap\"". This segment addresses the development of an Ubuntu Robotics ecosystem using Snaps and Ubuntu Core and its implications for production robot software deployment. Canonical has developed an Ubuntu Robotics ecosystem utilizing Snaps and Ubuntu Core, providing atomic updates and version linking for reliable robot deployment, incorporating ROS 2 extensions, observability hooks, and fleet management tools. However, there is limited discussion within the ROS 2 community regarding the use of Snaps for shipping production robot software, as alternatives such as standard apt, Docker, or Yocto remain more frequently discussed. The investigation examines whether strict confinement imposes limitations on necessary hardware access or if the maintenance overhead favors alternative deployment methodologies for robotics. This development signals ongoing technical debate regarding the most efficient deployment strategies for complex robotic systems.

items.title: Atlas Battery Pack to Use 70 Samsung SDI Cells, Report Says
items.summary: Atlas uses 70 Samsung SDI 2170 cells to form a battery pack with approximately 1.3 kWh of capacity. Samsung SDI is reportedly supplying most of the initial cells, with LG Energy Solution also involved in the supply chain. The reported cells have a capacity of 5,000 mAh each. Runtime depends on various factors including task demands, payload, and computing needs, not just pack capacity. Future solutions focus on battery swapping and new chemistries to improve humanoid robot operational duration.

Each of these reported cells possesses a capacity of five thousand milliampere-hours. Runtime for the robot is contingent upon factors such as task demands, payload, and computing requirements, rather than solely on the pack's total capacity. Future developments in this area are focusing on battery swapping and the exploration of novel chemistries to extend humanoid robot operational duration. This development signals ongoing research into power solutions for advanced artificial intelligence hardware.

items.title: Tau Robotics sends humanoids into homes for paid cleaning
items.summary: Tau Robotics offers paid humanoid cleaning services in San Francisco, utilizing remote human operators for much of the work while collecting training data. The service charges around $60 weekly for two robots, and trials revealed heavy dependence on reliable communication and operator equipment. The robots are four and a half feet tall with cameras for remote operation and use kinematic guidance for tasks like making beds. Initial trials demonstrated operational difficulties, including struggles with stairs and equipment shutdowns dependent on human assistance. The goal is to use these real-world examples to train models for more autonomous housekeeping.

items.title: Boston Dynamics built Stretch Gen 2 for reliable, consistent performance
items.summary: Boston Dynamics unveiled Stretch Gen 2, an updated autonomous mobile trailer unloading robot designed for enhanced reliability and performance. The new model features a modular design for easy part swaps, improved durability through automotive-grade connectors, and continuous rotation joints. Upgrades include a gripper that allows for multi-box picking in a single motion, reducing service time to just hours. The robot also incorporates onboard diagnostics and a continuously improving software platform that allows for remote performance enhancements. Customers have responded positively, finding the robot's user experience simple and effective for heavy lifting tasks.

items.title: Physicl raises $10M to make the digital world real enough for robots
items.summary: Physicl raised $10 million in seed funding to utilize its expertise in 3D rendering to improve robot training through realistic simulations. The company aims to help model designers and robot builders solve training problems by creating more accurate digital environments. Physicl offers tools, like Studio, that allow users to generate synthetic data for training robots on complex scenarios. The platform seeks to automate the process of transforming unstructured real-world information into high-fidelity 3D representations for AI. This approach aims to enable robots to better understand, interact with, and manipulate physical space.

items.title: Inside Unitree's Hangzhou Factory, Robots Are Still Mostly Built by Hand
items.summary: Most of Unitree's robot actuator production in the Hangzhou factory remains largely manual, with only a few new automated lines present. The company's 2025 filings indicate that direct labor accounted for only 8.1% of the cost of goods. The author argues that US trade barriers make factory automation more valuable to American makers than to Unitree. Automation is expected to increase significantly as AI reduces the time needed for programming and integration. Investment focus should shift to building standardized motor lines rather than solely focusing on humanoid assembly.

items.title: Embodied AI unveils AIR humanoid robot for shared factory work
items.summary: Embodied AI has introduced the AIR humanoid robot for shared factory work, with manufacturer testing currently in progress. AIR is designed to handle repetitive manual tasks that change frequently, unlike conventional automation. The robot utilizes a tendon-driven architecture with motors in the torso and wheels for stability on factory floors, prioritizing manipulation over bipedal mobility. The AI learns tasks by observing runs, allowing for human oversight during the learning phase. Physical reliability is a central design requirement, and CE marking is planned for 2027.

items.title: Team Chiron Competes in DARPA Triage Challenge Finals
items.summary: Team Chiron uses autonomous drones and ground robots with AI to assess and triage wounded individuals during disasters. The system gathers data on casualties by detecting vital signs and locating injured people from a distance, aiming to help emergency responders prioritize care. This technology is being developed through participation in the DARPA Triage Challenge. Team Chiron's goal is to provide a comprehensive picture of a disaster scene to facilitate faster and more informed medical decisions. The overall aim is to advance autonomous systems that improve emergency response efficiency and save lives.

items.title: Welcome, ByteDexter!
items.summary: ByteDexter is a five-finger robotic research hand developed by ByteDance Seed for AI research. It is designed with an emphasis on dexterity, compact integration, and tactile sensing, featuring electric motors within the palm. The hand utilizes rigid mechanical linkages and passive four-bar linkages for finger movement. Tactile arrays measure normal force, and its performance is rated as 4/5 for degrees of freedom but only 1/5 for strength. As a prototype, it is part of the GR Dexter project, aiming to advance AI systems for robots with humanlike hands.

items.title: Welcome, REX G1!
items.summary: REX G1 is RoboScience's first wheeled humanoid robot, designed for environments like factories and homes, standing 170 cm tall and weighing 80 kg. It features an adjustable torso, two articulated arms capable of supporting a 10 kg load, and a working reach of 0.1 to 2 meters. The robot has a maximum speed of 5 km/h, operates for four hours on a charge, and includes safety brakes on all joints. Its demonstrated capabilities focus on obstacle avoidance and sorting goods, reflecting an early stage of development.

The robot stands 175 cm tall, weighs 120 kg, and has a listed strength of 12 kg. Its demonstrated tasks include obstacle avoidance, sorting goods, and operating a dishwasher. The robot is a research platform focused on mobile manipulation in domestic assistance settings.

items.title: Welcome, Gento Luna!
items.summary: Gento Luna is a wheeled humanoid robot featuring a folding structure that reduces its height from 170 cm to 79 cm. It weighs 90 kg and possesses 26 degrees of freedom, with each arm having seven degrees of freedom and a 6 kg lifting capacity. The robot is equipped with 3D LiDAR for obstacle avoidance and articulated arms for sorting goods and folding clothes. It utilizes force-controlled electric joints with compliant impedance control for physical interaction. Luna is currently listed as a prototype with a skill score of 3 out of 10, targeting applications in commercial services and education.

items.title: Ep#115: Delta-0 (Δ₀): A New Chapter in Humanoid Intelligence
items.summary: Delta-0 is a humanoid foundation model capable of long-horizon, whole-body locomotion and manipulation using generalist policies trained on whole-body human data. It achieves this by jointly designing the policy and controller, utilizing a delta action space for seamless human intervention during execution. The model demonstrates impressive abilities in everyday tasks like operating a turntable, making the bed, and interacting with objects by coordinating movement and force. The research emphasizes that long-horizon loco-manipulation is challenging due to the coupled control, perception, and dynamic nature of the environment. Key design principles include whole-body control, execution fidelity, and compliance to enable reliable real-world deployment.

The research demonstrates the model's ability to achieve complex everyday tasks such as operating a turntable and making the bed through coordinated movement and force interaction with objects. This was accomplished by jointly designing the policy and controller, employing a delta action space to allow for seamless human intervention during execution. The study highlights that long-horizon loco-manipulation presents significant challenges due to the coupled control, perception, and dynamic nature of the environment, emphasizing the importance of whole-body control and execution fidelity for reliable deployment. This advancement indicates a significant step toward more capable and adaptable embodied artificial intelligence systems.

items.title: Industry experts discuss China blocking SoftBank acquisition of ABB Robotics
items.summary: China blocked SoftBank's acquisition of ABB Robotics due to concerns that training data for AI models could be transferred overseas. This action stems from regulatory worries regarding the transfer of robotics data, which is now viewed as strategically important for physical AI development. Other countries are also taking action to protect sovereign physical AI, with examples including U.S. bans on certain autonomous robots. The issue highlights growing concerns about robotics data, intellectual property, and local manufacturing capabilities in cross-border mergers. Ultimately, the situation reflects broader geopolitical tensions concerning the convergence of automation, data, and artificial intelligence.
